entries.title: Poole Borough Council v GN
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: A public authority does not owe a duty of care merely by exercising its statutory functions; liability requires an assumption of responsibility or a special relationship.
entries.facts: A claim by children who suffered abuse in foster care against the local authority.
entries.holding: A public authority does not owe a duty of care merely by exercising its statutory functions; liability requires an assumption of responsibility or a special relationship.

entries.title: Robinson v Chief Constable of West Yorkshire Police
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: The police owe a duty of care in the ordinary way when their positive conduct creates a foreseeable risk of injury; the Caparo test applies to novel categories, not to established ones.
entries.facts: A bystander was injured during a police chase of a suspect.
entries.holding: The police owe a duty of care in the ordinary way when their positive conduct creates a foreseeable risk of injury.

entries.title: Michael v Chief Constable of South Wales Police
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: The police owe no duty of care to protect an individual from the criminal acts of a third party in the absence of an assumption of responsibility or a special relationship.
entries.facts: A claim by the family of a woman murdered by her ex-partner after police failures.
entries.holding: The police owe no duty of care to protect an individual from the criminal acts of a third party in the absence of an assumption of responsibility or a special relationship.

entries.title: Caparo Industries plc v Dickman
entries.principle: A duty of care arises only where damage is reasonably foreseeable, the relationship is sufficiently proximate, and it is fair, just and reasonable to impose the duty.
entries.facts: Shareholders relied on an auditor's report to buy shares; the company collapsed and they sued the auditors.
entries.holding: A duty of care arises only where damage is reasonably foreseeable, the relationship is sufficiently proximate, and it is fair, just and reasonable to impose the duty.

entries.title: Hill v Chief Constable of West Yorkshire
entries.principle: The police owe no general duty of care to individual members of the public in the investigation and suppression of crime; policy considerations preclude such a duty.
entries.facts: A claim by the mother of a victim of the Yorkshire Ripper against the police.
entries.holding: The police owe no general duty of care to individual members of the public in the investigation and suppression of crime; policy considerations preclude such a duty.

entries.title: Donoghue v Stevenson
entries.principle: A manufacturer owes a duty of care to the ultimate consumer to take reasonable care that goods are free from defects likely to cause injury, the neighbour principle being the foundation of the tort.
entries.facts: A consumer became ill after drinking ginger beer containing a decomposed snail; she sued the manufacturer.
entries.holding: A manufacturer owes a duty of care to the ultimate consumer to take reasonable care that goods are free from defects likely to cause injury.
